stories.headline: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.title: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.summary: Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday exhorted MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises) to look beyond domestic markets and take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs (Free Trade Agreements).
In his address at the SME Finance & Investment Summit, Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs.
This is remarkably low compared with 60–70 per cent utilisation by partner countries’ exports to India.
“It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table.
Learn about the FTAs relevant to your products, invest in quality, standards and certification, and draw on the support available from the agencies concerned,” he said.
The Governor highlighted the importance of formalising the financials of MSMEs and earning the confidence of their lenders.
“Every lasting business relationship rests on trust.
Customers stay with you because you deliver quality on time; suppliers stay with you because you keep your commitments.
Lenders are no different.
“You will obtain credit on better terms if you keep proper accounts, file returns on time, transact digitally and manage your finances with discipline.
Increasingly, the data trail your business leaves behind will count for as much as the assets you can pledge,” he said.
Malhotra encouraged the MSMEs to use the instruments built for them and treat support as a catalyst, not a crutch.

stories.headline: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.title: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 27: National Conference (NC) Rajya Sabha MP Chowdry Mohammad Ramzan recorded 91 per cent attendance, participated in 21 debates and raised 32 questions during his first three parliamentary sessions, with issues concerning Jammu and Kashmir’s infrastructure, employment, agriculture and environmental security featuring prominently in his parliamentary interventions. According to parliamentary performance data compiled by PRS Legislative Research, Ramzan’s attendance stood 11 percentage points above the national average of 80 per cent and four percentage points above Jammu and Kashmir’s average of 87 per cent. Ramzan, who took oath on December 1, 2025, participated in the Winter Session of 2025, followed by the Budget and Monsoon sessions of 2026, covering 45 parliamentary sittings up to August 13, 2026. His parliamentary participation came despite disruptions during the Monsoon Session, which affected the conduct of parliamentary business. Among the key issues raised by the MP were the construction of the Sadhna and Razdan Pass tunnels, all-weather connectivity to isolated border regions, the proposed Sopore-Kupwara railway link, extension of the Baramulla railway line and the Bandipora-Lolab road project. Ramzan also sought details from the Centre on stalled bridge and tunnel projects in rural Jammu and Kashmir, road connectivity between Machil and Tangdhar via Keran, and the inclusion of Bungus Valley under the National Ropeways Development Programme. Employment and economic concerns featured prominently in his parliamentary questions, with the MP seeking details regarding a special employment package for Jammu and Kashmir, safeguards for horticultural crops in view of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and the promotion of high-density plantations. During parliamentary proceedings, Ramzan raised concerns over the threat to Kashmir’s horticulture industry from harmful agrochemicals and apple imports, besides flagging issues concerning hydroelectric power projects, particularly in the Chenab Valley. On environmental and public welfare issues, the MP sought information regarding Jammu and Kashmir’s vulnerability to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the drinking water crisis, drug addiction surveys and seizures, and micro-irrigation facilities. His parliamentary interventions also covered school education infrastructure, telecom services, tourism promotion in Kupwara, the status and completion timeline of Government Medical College Handwara and the operationalisation of the Khelo India Excellence Centre at Gulmarg. Beyond region-specific matters, Ramzan participated in discussions on the Union Budget 2026–27, the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address, the functioning of the Ministry of Rural Development and several legislative proposals. These included Bills concerning public examinations, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Central Armed Police Forces, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the strength of Supreme Court judges. Through Special Mentions and other parliamentary interventions, Ramzan also raised the demand for granting classical language status to Kashmiri, the attack on former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, the need to uphold communal harmony and the safety and evacuation of Indian nationals from Gulf countries.

stories.title: Only 5% Of Indian MSMEs Use Core AI & Just 20-30% Tap FTA Tariff Cuts | Sanjay Malhotra
stories.summary: "Being small should not mean thinking small." A strong wake-up call for Indian MSMEs highlights how scaling up, adopting artificial intelligence, and tapping Free Trade Agreements can transform India’s growth trajectory. Raising MSME productivity to top global levels could add a massive 11% to India’s GDP, especially with revised classification limits removing the fear of losing policy benefits. stories.title: Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri Appointed Jammu and Kashmir Advocate General
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 27 : The Jammu and Kashmir Government on Friday appointed Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri as the new Advocate General of the Union Territory. The Formal order appointing Qadri was issued on Friday after the Raj Bhavan cleared his name for the post. Three names; Advocate Faisal Qadri, Advocate Ishaq Qadri and Advocate Seema Shekhar had been sent to the Raj Bhavan for consideration for the top legal position. Qadri's appointment was formalised following the clearance from the Raj Bhavan.

opening: Srinagar, Nov 27: The Jammu and Kashmir Government on Friday appointed Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri as the new Advocate General of the Union Territory.
The Formal order appointing Qadri was issued on Friday after the Raj Bhavan cleared his name for the post.

Srinagar, Nov 27: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha has approved the appointment of senior advocate Faisal Qadri as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir.
Qadri will serve as the government's chief legal adviser and represent the Union Territory in legal matters before the High Court and other courts.
The appointment fills the position of Advocate General, which had remained vacant since October 2024.
Qadri is a senior advocate practising before the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.

The appointment was notified by the Department of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs through Government Order S.O. 329, issued by order of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha under Section 79(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
The notification, signed by Commissioner/Secretary to the Government Achal Sethi, lays down the terms of appointment, remuneration, allowances and professional fees payable to the Advocate General.
Under the order, Qadri will receive a monthly remuneration of ₹1 lakh and will be entitled to rent-free furnished accommodation at either Jammu or Srinagar.
If he opts to reside in his own house, he will receive a compensatory allowance of ₹12,000 per month.
He will also be provided an official vehicle free of charge for use within and outside city limits, besides a monthly sumptuary allowance of ₹3,000.
The order provides for medical reimbursement and travel allowances at the rates admissible to a sitting Judge of the High Court.
His headquarters will be the same as that of the High Court, unless otherwise directed by the government.
The Home Department will provide him security as required.
Fee structure for court appearances.
The notification also prescribes a detailed fee structure for the Advocate General's professional work.
For each contested writ petition, appeal, suit or civil appeal conducted on behalf of the Union Territory before the High Court, Qadri will receive a fee of ₹5,000.

For appearances before the Supreme Court, Delhi High Court and other courts and tribunals outside Jammu and Kashmir, the fee has been fixed at ₹50,000 for each effective hearing and ₹5,000 for each non-effective hearing.
He will also be paid ₹50,000 per conference in cases before the Supreme Court and Delhi High Court.
In arbitration matters within the Union Territory, the prescribed fee will be ₹10,000 per effective hearing and ₹3,000 per non-effective hearing.
For arbitration cases outside the UT, the rates will be ₹25,000 and ₹5,000, respectively.

The order clarifies that no separate fee will be payable for providing legal opinions to the government, attending meetings or consultations with government functionaries or bodies wholly owned or controlled by it, or appearing before the High Court in criminal and contempt cases.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday disposed of a Public Interest Litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking directions to authorities to put in place measures enabling legal heirs to trace and claim unclaimed financial assets, including bank deposits, shares and mutual fund investments.

Noting that the Union Government, the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India have taken various administrative and regulatory steps to address the issue, the bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice R Mahadevan observed that judicial directions in that regard are not necessary.
At the same time, the bench placed on record its appreciation for Dalal for taking up a genuine public cause, saying that the case was an example of a responsible use of public interest litigation.
The bench also appreciated Advocate Prashant Bhushan for espousing the petitioners' cause with "passion and perseverance."

"The present proceedings were instituted not for securing any personal benefit but with the objective of protecting the financial interests of countless depositors, investors and their lawful claimants.
The petitioner has consistently drawn attention to the difficulties faced by ordinary citizens in identifying and recovering the unclaimed financial assets.
The concerns raised were genuine and the pursuit of the appropriate institutional measures to address them reflects a responsible exercise of public interest litigation," the bench observed.
However, the Court noted that the principal concerns raised have been substantially addressed by measures undertaken by the respondents (SEBI, RBI and the Department of Economic Affairs).

"We take on record the statements and assurances made in the respondents affidavits and expect the concerned authorities to continue the efforts towards improving the accessibility, efficiency, and transparency of the mechanism for identifying and recovering unclaimed financial assets.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the petition pending for further monitoring of the regulatory measures already undertaken.
Any specific grievances concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law," the bench added.
The bench had reserved judgment on November 17.
